result.summary: Sets the SO_OOBINLINE socket option on TCP sockets to deliver out-of-band urgent data inline through regular recv() calls. Adds a functional test to verify that TCP urgent data is received inline.
result.problem: TCP urgent data is ignored by regular recv() calls, causing socket polling using select() on certain operating systems to repeatedly flag unread data as pending. Even though PR 36665 stopped this condition from halting node progress or crashing, the unresolved pending state remains an unnecessary divergence in socket handling across platforms.
evidence: PR description: 'There is currently nothing preventing us to receive TCP urgent data, which would never be returned by recv(). Linux's poll() is indifferent to this, but the select() socket monitoring may keep reporting it as pending on some platforms.'
PR description: Cites lessons from a recent TCP OOM vulnerability advisory to 'reduce the amount of custom logic for less well-tested platforms.'
result.scope_notes: Small two-commit change (+45/-0) adding the socket option and a QA test.
result.card: Sets the SO_OOBINLINE socket option on TCP sockets so out-of-band urgent data is processed inline through standard recv() calls rather than skipped. On platforms relying on select(), unread urgent data could previously trigger persistent socket event loops. Delivering urgent bytes inline allows Bitcoin Core's P2P parsing logic to see the irregular bytes and disconnect misbehaving peers directly.

risk.why: Modifying socket options across operating systems could cause socket configuration errors or unintended connection drops across the P2P network.
